source_documents.title: Excited State Intramolecular Proton Transfer‐Mediated Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Behavior of Hexapole Hydrogen Bonding Molecule

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emission intensity increased under an argon atmosphere, and the degassed sample solution showed a long-lived component with a time constant of 15 μs.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1

reference_evidence_units.quote: Variable temperature lifetime measurements suggested that phosphorescence disappears at 160 K, and thermally activated delayed fluorescence is observed at elevated temperatures.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Phosphorescence at low temperature, TADF at higher temperature.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Theoretical calculations revealed that all-keto form 1A is photoexcited, generating 1B* after one proton transfer, and thermally activated delayed fluorescence is observed via reverse intersystem crossing from higher-lying triplet states (T2 and T3) to the singlet state (S1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Single ESIPT 1A*→1B*, then TADF via rISC from T2/T3.
